title: Bend Elementary School Shooting: Authorities Identify Victims, Teen Gunman, and Hero Bystander
snippet: Police in Bend, Oregon, have released the identities of a kindergarten student, a beloved special education teacher, and the 16-year-old shooter following Thursday's tragic massacre at Silver Rail Elementary School.
content:
BEND, Ore. — Police on Friday officially identified the victims and gunman involved in Thursday's deadly mass shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School, offering a tragic breakdown of a minutes-long rampage that left four dead before an armed community member intervened to end the bloodshed.

Authorities identified two of the deceased victims as 5-year-old student Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old special education teacher Megan Lambert. Two other young boys, aged 8 and 11, were also killed in the attack; their names are being withheld at the request of their families. A 7-year-old girl remains in serious but stable condition at Oregon Health & Science University, while 54-year-old teacher Becky Drury is recovering from surgery for serious arm and hand injuries.

A Community Remembers a Beloved Teacher and Young Student

For Lambert, teaching at Silver Rail was the fulfillment of a lifelong dream. In a statement released Friday, her family remembered the Bend native as a passionate educator with a huge heart who constantly advocated for children with special needs.

"Silver Rail was her first job as a teacher... This was her dream job," her family said. "Megan was compassionate and had a huge heart. She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs."

Police Chief Mike Krantz confirmed that all four deceased victims were inside a special education classroom when the suspect opened fire. No other students were present in the classroom at the time.

Moments of Bravery Amid the Horror

Police identified the shooter as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, a former Silver Rail student who had previously received special education services. Officials stated John approached the school around 1:00 p.m., threw a 12-gauge pump-action shotgun over a perimeter fence, and breached the property.

After firing at a passing pickup truck whose driver confronted him, John shot out the glass of an exterior door to force his way into the building. Once inside, he fired up to 15 rounds into the classroom.

The tragedy could have been significantly worse if not for the quick thinking of staff and a brave bystander. Before help arrived, one teacher in the classroom threw her cell phone at John and tackled him, physically fighting to disarm him.

Simultaneously, local resident Kaylub Giamanco, 36, who witnessed the shooter fire at the pickup truck outside, grabbed his personal handgun and followed the teenager into the building. Giamanco entered the shattered exterior doors, found the teacher grappling with John, and shot the gunman, killing him instantly. Police confirmed John was carrying an additional 44 rounds of ammunition when he was brought down.

"I don't think we can underestimate or underappreciate [his] courage," Chief Krantz said of Giamanco. "When someone is willing to risk their own life for others, we recognize that. The quick thinking to follow someone into the school is incredible, and undoubtedly saved people."

Motive Remains Under Investigation

While federal and local law enforcement officers continue to analyze evidence gathered from John's home, authorities admitted a clear motive has not yet been established. Sources close to the investigation indicated the shotgun used in the attack was purchased by the suspect's mother in August.

"Everyone wants to know why, including us," Chief Krantz told reporters. "We may never get that full answer, but we want it."

On Thursday evening, thousands of Bend residents gathered at Drake Park for a candlelight vigil. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek addressed the mourning crowd, offering condolences on behalf of the state. Mental health officials confirmed that free grief counseling services are actively being provided across Deschutes County to help students, staff, and families process the profound loss.
